 Villa Ginori, Versilia home of marquis Puccini dedicated La Bohème to, goes on market
 Neo-Gothic residence overlooks Lake Massaciuccoli
 FLORENCE ,
 28 October 2026, 09:34
 ANSA English Desk
 Share
 Link copiato 
 - ALL RIGHTS RESERVED
 Villa Ginori, a historic residence in the coastal Versilia area of Tuscany, in the province of Lucca, has gone onto the market with Lionard Luxury Real Estate ( https://www.lionard.com/exclusive-historic-villa-on-lake-versil ia-hinterland.htm l). 
    The home once belonged to Marquis Carlo Ginori Lisci, heir to the celebrated Ginori porcelain factory at Doccia and a close friend of Giacomo Puccini, who dedicated La Bohème to him. 
    Overlooking Lake Massaciuccoli in Massarosa, the villa remains in the hands of descendants of the Ginori Lisci family. 
    It preserves rooms once frequented by the composer, who lived across the lake in Torre del Lago, as well as Liberty-style decorations by Francesco Fanelli, a painter who studied under Giovanni Fattori. 
    The estate owes its present appearance to Carlo Ginori Lisci. In 1887, the marquis acquired Lake Massaciuccoli and the surrounding land from the Minutoli family, transforming an existing building into a residence in the Tuscan neo-Gothic style. 
    The villa's architectural character is defined by its direct relationship with the water. The lake extends beneath the building's great arches to a private covered boathouse, making it possible to reach the residence directly by boat. 
    The same relationship continues inside, where the large windows of the loggia and winter garden open onto the lake. Irises, botanical motifs and Oriental-inspired lines by Fanelli, who was asked in 1900 by the marquis to decorate several rooms, echo the surrounding landscape across the walls. 
    The estate comprises approximately 4,000 square metres of built space across eight buildings and 10 hectares of private land. 
    Alongside the main villa, which measures about 1,200 square metres, stand an 800-square-metre 19th-century residence and a clubhouse created from a former boat shelter, as well as a chapel, a limonaia and other service buildings. 
    The park, dotted with historic palm trees and exotic botanical species, is crossed by navigable canals. 
    "The most authentic expression of Made in Italy is not only what we produce, but also what we have been able to build, preserve and pass on," said Dimitri Corti, Founder and CEO of Lionard Luxury Real Estate. 
    "Villa Ginori represents a dimension of luxury that goes beyond the material value of a property. A building can be restored, transformed and adapted to new needs. What cannot be recreated is its history, its relationship with the people who lived there, and with the land to which it belongs. That is what makes certain places truly irreplaceable."
